title: Making decisions with if
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to compare values and use if, elif and else to choose what your program does.

sections.title: Comparing values
sections.text: A comparison asks a question that is True or False. Python uses == (equal), != (not equal), < and > (less and more), and <= and >= (or equal). Remember that = stores a value, while == checks if two values are the same.

sections.title: if and indentation
sections.text: if runs some lines only when a condition is True. The if line ends with a colon, and the lines that belong to it are indented by 4 spaces. When the indentation ends, the program carries on as normal.

sections.title: elif and else
sections.text: elif means "else if" and adds another check. else catches everything that did not match. Python checks from the top and runs only the first block whose condition is True.

sections.title: and, or
sections.text: and is True only when both sides are True: age >= 11 and age <= 15. or is True when at least one side is True: day == "Sat" or day == "Sun".

diagram.title: How if, elif and else choose
steps: If True, run its block and skip the rest
If False, check the next elif
If nothing is True, run else

check_questions.explanation: 12 >= 13 is False, so Python skips the if block and runs the else block.

misconception.0: 12 is not 13 or more, so the condition is False.
misconception.2: Only one of the if block or the else block runs, never both.
misconception.3: When the if is False, the else block runs.

check_questions.explanation: 7 is more than 5 and less than 10, so the first condition is True. Python runs that block and skips the rest.

misconception.0: The elif is only checked when the first condition is False.
misconception.1: Python stops after the first True condition.
misconception.3: else only runs when nothing above it is True.

check_questions.prompt: Which symbol checks whether two values are the same?
check_questions.explanation: == compares two values and gives True or False.

misconception.0: = stores a value in a variable. It does not compare.
misconception.1: != checks that two values are different.
misconception.2: => is not a Python operator. Greater than or equal is written >=.
